set.note: Named after Italian economist Vilfredo Pareto, who studied how unevenly wealth and income were spread. A rule of thumb, not a law.

why: The '80% of Italy's land owned by 20%' anecdote is widely repeated but not reliably documented in Pareto's work (his studies were of income/wealth distributions); replace with a verifiable statement.

set.def: invisible material, detected only through its gravity, that astronomers estimate outweighs ordinary matter about five to one

why: The ~5:1 ratio (Planck: ~27% vs ~5%) is against all ordinary (baryonic) matter, most of which is not visible; 'visible material' would make the ratio far larger.

set.def: a wealthy West African state that flourished from the 1200s to the 1500s, famed for its gold and its scholarly city, Timbuktu

why: End date 'the 1600s' conflicts with Britannica (13th-16th century); the empire had collapsed to a rump by c.1600. Use the dates the sources agree on.

set.why: Archaeological research proved local Africans built it, refuting colonial-era claims that foreigners must have built the site.

why: The walls themselves did not 'disprove' anything; it was archaeological excavation (Randall-MacIver 1905, Caton-Thompson 1929) that refuted the colonial claims.

ex: Scientists have cooled atoms to within a tiny fraction of a degree of absolute zero.
The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero, so water freezes at about 273 kelvins.

why: 'No temperature in kelvins is ever negative' is contradicted by experimentally realized negative absolute temperatures (e.g., Braun et al. 2013); replaced with a safe fact. Level 5 is a big miss for a widely known concept.
Level 5 ('well-read') is a big miss; Einstein's relativity and E = mc² are general adult knowledge (~2-3).

ex: In One Hundred Years of Solitude, magical realism lets a young woman rise into the sky while folding sheets.
Toni Morrison's Beloved is often read as magical realism, bringing a ghost into a story about slavery's aftermath.

why: Stated flatly that Beloved 'uses magical realism'; Morrison herself rejected the label, so attribute it as a common reading.

set.def: the study of chemical tags on DNA and its packaging that switch genes on or off without changing the DNA sequence

why: Epigenetic marks include histone modifications on DNA's packaging proteins, not only tags on DNA itself.

set.def: the movement of water through a semipermeable membrane from a weaker solution into a more concentrated one

why: Osmosis requires a semipermeable (selectively permeable) membrane; any membrane is inaccurate.
'autonomy' and 'self-rule' usually denote limited self-government within a larger state, i.e., the opposite of full sovereignty; not true synonyms.

ex: Negligence, such as injuring someone by running a red light, is one kind of tort.
Aisha took a course in tort law covering negligence, defamation, and product liability.

why: Original example was ungrammatical ('Negligence is one kind of tort, such as a driver...' attaches the example to 'tort').

set.why: Developed by Charles Sanders Peirce, William James, and John Dewey, it influenced American education, law, and psychology.

why: Peirce founded pragmatism; James popularized and Dewey extended it. 'Founded by' all three contradicts the item's own cloze ('Peirce founded ___').

set.def: Descartes's statement “I think, therefore I am,” meaning that the very act of thinking, even doubting, proves one's own existence

why: Descartes's argument rests on thinking in general (of which doubting is one form), not doubting alone.
ML is a type of AI; 'artificial intelligence' also fits the cloze ('engineers used ___ so the system could pick up spam patterns').
QE is itself a monetary-policy tool; overlapping definitions.
QE is a form of monetary policy, so 'monetary policy' can arguably answer 'which term means a central bank creating money to buy bonds'.
Dopamine is also a hormone and both are 'chemical messengers'; too close for 'Dopamine is a ___'.
MS is an inflammatory disease; 'inflammation' can be read as fitting the cloze.
An LLM is a neural network; 'the neural network could summarize reports and draft emails' fits the cloze.
'connects to a mapping service's IP address' is literally sensible in the cloze.
'rocks along the Ring of Fire suddenly slipped' is semi-plausible in the cloze.
Partition was part of decolonization; 'during the decolonization' could fill the 1947 cloze.
'In the novel's surrealism/allegory, no one is surprised when flowers rain from the sky' can be read as sensible.
The Socratic method is the dialectic of Plato's dialogues (the item's own example); overlapping meaning.
'Critics of Descartes's metaphysics asked how a nonphysical soul could move a physical arm' is a sensible sentence.
A careless reader can take 'a balloon zooming forward is a classic demonstration of kinetic energy' as correct.
